So this is stale wiring, not a deliberate two-contract split, and the bump's whole blast radius is one nullable field plus the `element:` segment of BuildVersionStamp (1 -> 2).

The doc already named v2 as the SSOT before any of this: docs/architecture/actor-hud-ideal.md:234 says 'element-catalog.v2.json owns each concrete glyph kind and colour', and §4.1's forbidden-then-replace table requires the renderer to accept only the catalog-declared visual vocabulary. The Server was the reader that did not know that yet.

TEST DESIGN — why the assertions are shaped the way they are, and what each one can and cannot catch. The route is a pure read of static hubs, so the test harness injects the catalogs itself and a route-only assertion would have stayed green with Program.cs reverted to v1. Three assertions, each with a distinct failure to catch: (1) the Server and Injector readers must name the SAME file — a cross-host agreement contract, asserted as a relationship rather than the literal 'v2', so a future v3 that moves both hosts stays green and a one-sided move fails; (2) the file both hosts read must actually carry glyph data — the anti-vacuity assertion, without which (1) would be satisfied by both hosts reading v1; (3) the served DTO must carry those values — this is what fails if BuildDto drops the field. Nothing pins a row count, a glyph count, or a glyph name.

The pre-existing harness line `ElementSurfaceCatalogLoader.Parse(ReadTuning("element-catalog.v1.json"))` in ActorSurfaceEndpointsTests.cs is itself the bug reproduced in miniature: it mirrored the composition root's stale revision, so every route assertion in the file was reasoning about a catalog production never served. It is changed to read whatever file Program.cs names, with the reason recorded in the code and the commit message — that is a pre-existing test encoding v1 as correct, which is the case the brief says is the thing to fix.

FOUND, NOT FIXED, routed to actor-hud-element-icons-20260917: exactly one of seven rows declares no hudGlyph — `omni`, whose `presentationOnly` is true. Both data/tuning/** and the Core/Injector HUD trees are outside my fence, so this is a report, not an edit. Note also that guard hardcodes 'element-catalog.v2.json' as a literal path, which is why the anti-vacuity assertion here is expressed against 'the file the readers name' rather than against v2.
